what: /restart is the skill CC fires on itself when the session should come back on a new build. It runs three steps in a fixed order and no other. (1) MEASURE: `cairn cc restart status`, and the captured text is handed to skills/restart/selector.py, whose branch() returns exactly one of two words -- `now` when a line reads `inner loop: HOLDING (pid N)`, meaning a loop is behind this session and ending CC is safe, and `spawn` for everything else, meaning nothing behind this session may be killed so a second instance is stood up beside it. The branch is code rather than prose because a branch condition that lives only in prose is a branch nobody can red. (2) SAVE: /saveslate, fired as a skill so its door can verify the live git heads; any refusal aborts the restart outright. (3) HAND OFF: `cairn cc restart now` (which ends this conversation and lets the loop reopen it) or `cairn cc restart spawn` (which kills nothing and reports the new instance's tmux session and remote-control name).
why: Today the act is three commands a tired operator has to remember in the right order, and the order is the whole safety of it: measure, save, then relaunch. Getting it wrong in the other order is a session that ends with nothing written down. Akien, 2026-09-22: 'cairn restart and cairn cc.x restart and slash restart. We only need to have you around to supervise the process the first time.' The skill is the third name, and it is the one CC types.
invoke: /restart (from inside a CC session, when the session should come back on a new build)
